title: Jeremy Clarkson’s Ferrari 355 Is Headed to Auction

body_markdown:
Once a relatively affordable entry point into Prancing Horse ownership,[the Ferrari 355](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/your-handy-1994-99-ferrari-f355-buyers-guide/) is[going up in value](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/hagerty-price-guide/5-cars-gaining-value-in-a-split-market/) as younger buyers seek out the cars they grew up dreaming about. Many of these enthusiasts grew up watching *Top Gear* as well. British auction house Iconic Auctioneer has found the perfect overlap for those who fit in the center of that particular Venn diagram: It’s selling a 1996 Ferrari 355 GTS that was delivered new to Jeremy Clarkson.


Finished in Rosso Corsa and registered in England, this 355 GTS was purchased by Clarkson after he tested the then-new Ferrari and declared it “the greatest car in the world; ever.” The former *Top Gear* host configured it with the gated six-speed stick, a two-tone Crema and red interior, and optional sport seats. The term “sport seats” means different things to different carmakers. In the 355 cosmos, the sport seats represent one of the rarest and most sought-after options, and they usually increase a car’s value.


The original warranty card lists Clarkson as the original owner, according to Iconic Auctioneers. He took delivery of it in August 1996 and often wrote about it in *Sunday Times* columns. He notably retook (and failed) his driving test in the car in May 1999.

After putting about 6000 miles on it, Clarkson gave the car away through a contest organized by the *Sunday Times* . It then went through the hands of several collectors who drove it sparingly. Its odometer shows about 15,300 miles, which is low even for a classic Italian exotic car. We’re told that the 380-horsepower, 3.5-liter V-8 is original to the car and got a new timing belt in 2025.


Even if it wasn’t Jeremy Clarkson’s old car, this Ferrari 355 GTS has a good chance of commanding a premium because it ticks many of the right boxes: Low mileage, no major modifications, the six-speed stick, sport seats, and a thoroughly documented history. Celebrity ownership doesn’t guarantee a bump in value, but the Clarkson cachet certainly doesn’t hurt.


Iconic Auctioneers[estimates](https://www.iconicauctioneers.com/1996-ferrari-f355-rec17690-1-nec-1126) that Clarkson’s 355 will sell for between £200,000 and £250,000 (about $265,500 to $332,000) when it crosses the block in Birmingham, England, on November 14. For context, *[Hagerty](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/ferrari/f355/1996/1996-ferrari-f355-gts?id=aCn1I000000DDCmSAO&timeframe=5Y)* pegs the value of a good-condition 1996 355 GTS at up to about $258,000, while a concours-condition example is valued at $381,000 as of November 2026.
